A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EDM research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and supplementary materials are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original EDM results for relative pose estimation, homography estimation and visual localization, alongside ablations, runtime measurements and supplementary experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds experiments on batching, computational resources, another pose-estimation protocol and additional diagnostic examples.

M1.justification: The backbone, Correlation Injection Module, coarse matching, bidirectional axis-based refinement and training losses remain unchanged. The added negative log-likelihood experiment is an ablation, while the new regression diagrams explain the existing method.

E1.justification: MegaDepth, ScanNet, HPatches, InLoc and Aachen coverage is retained. Section 8.2 and Figure 11 add explicit qualitative failure scenarios involving extreme scale and viewpoint differences, extending the documented input conditions beyond the earlier successful matching examples.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds SuperPoint + LightGlue to the HPatches comparison, although this combination already appeared in other v1 experiments. New Table 13 evaluates JamMa alongside EDM, LoFTR and EfficientLoFTR. The original benchmark comparator sets otherwise remain intact.

E3.justification: The efficiency evaluation expands substantially: Table 5 distinguishes mixed-precision and FP32 timings, Table 11 varies inference batch size from 1 to 32, and Table 12 adds parameter, FLOP and memory metrics. Section 7.7 introduces an additional MegaDepth protocol using 832×832 inputs and PoseLib LO-RANSAC with a 0.5-pixel inlier threshold. These additions do not establish changes to the original training or benchmark protocols.

E4.justification: Table 7 adds a targeted focal-loss versus negative log-likelihood ablation. Timing analyses gain precision and batch-size comparisons, while Figures 10–11 add a detailed fine-matching case and failure examples. These extend the existing analyses without replacing the extensive original component ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seed variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. The predicted matching uncertainty sigma remains part of the existing model; its additional illustration does not introduce a new experimental uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: The original benchmark scores are retained, but substantial new results cover precision-specific latency, batching, resource consumption and LO-RANSAC evaluation. Table 7 adds the negative log-likelihood result of 56.3/71.9/83.2 AUC. Table 13 reports EDM at 64.7/77.8/86.8 versus JamMa at 64.1/77.4/86.5 under the new protocol; these are not same-setting improvements over v1. Table 5 also revises relative timing savings using its expanded precision comparisons.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 and the mathematical formulation are retained. The added regression illustrations and intuitive discussion introduce no new formal definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and stated methodological contributions retain their meaning. The conclusion narrows the performance claim from 'SOTA' to 'competitive,' and Figure 1 similarly replaces its higher-accuracy claim with competitive accuracy and lower latency.

C2.justification: Section 8.1 adds an interpretation that multimodal coordinate responses help correct imprecise maxima and illustrates confidence versus localization error. Section 8.2 explicitly identifies extreme scale/viewpoint differences as failure conditions. The resolution-dependent efficiency limitation already existed in v1's supplement and is relocated to the main text.

D1.justification: v2 documents precision-specific timings, batch-test hardware and input resolution, and the additional PoseLib LO-RANSAC preprocessing and threshold. These improve experimental specification. The architecture settings, optimizer, training schedule, hardware disclosures and stated code link otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Four references are added: Mamba, PoseLib, JamMa, and Learning to Make Keypoints Sub-Pixel Accurate. Section 7.7 positions EDM against JamMa's Mamba-based matcher and evaluation setup. The broader related-work organization and methodological positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording corrections, adds author email addresses and revises the conclusion. The supplement gains experiment and visualization subsections, while the former combined limitations/future-work section is redistributed. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: The visual presentation gains regression-paradigm diagrams, a detailed prediction/ground-truth visualization and failure images in Figures 9–11, plus new experimental displays in Tables 11–13. Figure 1 is redrawn with axis breaks and the already-tabulated RoMa and SuperPoint + LightGlue results. Table 5 gains separate precision entries, and Tables 2 and 7 gain rows.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the central efficiency argument more transparent through precision-specific comparisons and resource measurements, adds a contemporary JamMa comparison, and better explains the refinement mechanism and failure boundaries. Narrowing the blanket SOTA claim also improves calibration. These are useful, targeted improvements to an already substantial evaluation; the new LO-RANSAC scores do not demonstrate an improvement to EDM itself.
